'''Sophie Dabo-Niang''' (née ''Dabo'') is a [[Senegalese]] and [[France|French]] [[mathematician]], [[statistician]], and professor<ref name="AfricanWomen" /> who has done outreach to increase the status of African mathematicians.

==Biography==
===Early life===
Sophie was encouraged to pursue mathematics by her parents and her teachers. She knew she wanted to study mathematics early in high school.<ref name = "AfricanWomen">{{Cite web| title = Sophie Dabo {{!}} African Women in Mathematics Association| access-date = 2021-01-14| url = http://africanwomeninmath.org/fr/femmes-mathematiciennes/portrait/sophie-dabo}}</ref>

===Education===
Sophie Dabo-Niang earned her PhD in 2002 from the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] in [[Paris]].<ref name = "AfricanWomen" /> Sophie enjoys passing on her passion for mathematics to her students.<ref name="AfricanWomen" />

===Marriage and children===
As of 2016, Dabo-Niang is married.<ref name = "AfricanWomen" /> She had 3 children between starting her master's degree and finishing her doctoral thesis, and has 4 children in total.<ref name = "AfricanWomen" /><ref name = "YoutubeInterview">{{Cite AV media| people = Sciences & Coundefined (Director)| title = Egalité Hommes/Femmes au cœur des laboratoires scientifiques| accessdate = 2021-01-15| date = 2017-03-22| time = 2:50| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TQUfDXUpbbo}}</ref> She has said that balancing parenting and her mathematics career has been a challenge, and she credits her persistence to her desire to succeed and the support of her husband.<ref name = "AfricanWomen" />

==Mathematical work==
Dabo-Niang has published articles on [[Functional data analysis|functional statistics]], [[nonparametric statistics|nonparametric]] and semi-parametric estimates of weakly independent processes, [[spatial statistics]], and [[mathematical epidemiology]].<ref>{{Cite web| title = Sophie DABO Contact, Faculty Profile - Université de Lille| work = Université de Lille| access-date = 2021-01-15| url = https://pro.univ-lille.fr/sophie-dabo2/contact/}}</ref>

Dabo-Niang serves as an editor of the journal [[Revista Colombiana de Estadística]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rev.Colomb.Estad. - Editorial board|url=http://www.scielo.org.co/revistas/rce/iedboard.htm|access-date=2021-01-15|website=www.scielo.org.co}}</ref><ref name="LEM report">{{Cite conference| publisher = Lille Économie Management| pages = 114| last = Vauzeilles| first = Jacqueline| title = Rapport d'activité du LEM| date = 2015| url = https://lem.univ-lille.fr/fileadmin/user_upload/laboratoires/lem/DocAdmin/new_-Rapport_d_activite_LEM_UMR_9221_2015-2018.pdf}}</ref> and is on the scientific committee of the [[Centre International de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées|Centre International de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées (CIMPA)]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Executive Team {{!}} CIMPA|url=https://www.cimpa.info/en/node/6191|access-date=2021-01-15|website=www.cimpa.info}}</ref>

===Professorship and developing country outreach===
Sophie Dabo-Niang has successfully supervised the doctoral theses of several students in Africa.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Catalogue SUDOC|url=http://www.sudoc.abes.fr/cbs/xslt/DB=2.1/SET=4/TTL=1//CMD?ACT=AND&TRM=%5C9001+Y&REMEMBERFORMVALUES=N&COOKIE=U10178,Klecteurweb,D2.1,Ee175bdfd-ab,I250,B341720009+,SY,QDEF,A%5C9008+1,,J,H2-26,,29,,34,,39,,44,,49-50,,53-78,,80-87,NLECTEUR+PSI,R208.80.154.81,FN|access-date=2021-01-15|website=www.sudoc.abes.fr}}</ref> As of January 2021 she is a full professor at the [[University of Lille]] and is supervising and co-supervising multiple African students.<ref name="AfricanWomen" /> She has taught master's-level statistics courses, including in Senegal.<ref name="AfricanWomen" />

She introduced the [[spatial statistics]] subfields to [[Gaston Berger University|a university in Dakar, Senegal]], and supervised the first Senegalese and Mauritanian doctoral students focusing on the field. She often participates on thesis juries in Africa.<ref name="AfricanWomen" />

Dabo-Niang has coordinated scientific events in Africa. In Senegal, she coordinated a [[Centre International de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées|CIMPA]] event and an event to encourage young girls in the mathematical sciences.<ref name="AfricanWomen" /> She serves as the chair of the Developing Countries Committee for the [[European Mathematical Society]].<ref name="LEM report" /><ref>{{Cite web|last=nickgill|date=2018-02-20|title=Members|url=https://nickpgill.github.io/emscdc/members|access-date=2021-01-15|website=EMS-CDC|language=en}}</ref>

==Honours, decorations, awards and distinctions==
The [[African Women in Mathematics Association]] has profiled Dabo-Niang. She was honored by [[Femmes et Mathématiques]] in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web| title = Mathématiciennes africaines Meeting Agenda| work = FEMMES ET MATHÉMATIQUES| format = Professional Organization| access-date = 2021-01-15| date = 2015-05-30| url = https://femmes-et-maths.fr/2015/05/07/mathematiciennes-africaines/}}</ref>
